events: A child's toy telephone rings twice on its own in the character's presence, though it’s not connected to anything.
The scent of burning cinnamon fills the character's room at midnight, but no source can be found.
A stranger gives the character a torn tarot card with 'The Tower' on it, then disappears into the crowd.
The character notices an old payphone ringing on a deserted street; when they answer, they hear only static and a faint lullaby.
A nearby streetlight flickers on and off in sync with the character’s heartbeat.
An old newspaper blows into the character’s feet, with a headline showing the date of their Embrace.
A graffiti artist paints the character’s exact likeness on a wall in an unfamiliar part of town.
A raven perches near the character, caws three times, and then drops a withered rose at their feet.
The character’s reflection lags slightly behind their movements in a darkened window.
They find a locked diary written in a language they’ve never seen before, but every now and then, a page becomes readable.
The clocks around the character consistently read 3:33 AM, regardless of the actual time.
A photo booth picture of the character appears on the ground, showing them with someone they don’t recognize.
A child's drawing of a house matches the character’s haven in eerie detail, despite no child having seen it.
The street signs around the character temporarily shift into ancient runes before returning to normal.
A stranger slips a folded note into their hand reading, 'You have until the 13th moon.'
A locked antique music box near the character begins to play on its own, stopping abruptly when they touch it.
They find an old coin in their pocket that they don’t remember acquiring, with an inscription in Latin reading, 'All things end.'
Their shadow briefly splits into three distinct figures before reuniting with them.
A car alarm goes off every time they pass a specific street corner, even if no car is present.
They wake up with dirt under their fingernails, though they have no recollection of digging or going outside.
A flower wilts and dies whenever the character approaches it, but blooms again as soon as they leave.
A trail of small white feathers seems to follow the character for a day, disappearing the next morning.
A whisper in a foreign language calls the character by name whenever they walk past reflective surfaces.
The character finds an empty envelope on their doorstep with a wax seal that has their clan symbol pressed into it.
A stranger bumps into them, apologizes, and says, 'See you soon,' though they’ve never met.
The streetlight nearest their haven never illuminates, remaining in a constant state of dimness.
The character encounters a stray dog with the same scar they have, staring at them knowingly.
The character's favorite book suddenly has all its page numbers replaced with the number 13.
A poster in an alley displays a distorted image of the character with the words 'Lost Soul' beneath.
The character hears faint church bells ringing, but there’s no church within miles.
An old-fashioned key appears under their pillow, though they don’t recognize the lock it belongs to.
The windows in a nearby abandoned building are all shattered except for one, which reflects only the character.
A mysterious person brushes past the character and whispers, 'They’re watching.'
When the character receives change, one coin bears their own face in profile instead of a historical figure.
They come across an abandoned coat that perfectly matches one they wore decades ago, right down to the wear and tear.
For a few hours, every door the character opens creaks out the first notes of an old, familiar lullaby.
An elderly man offers them a flower, only for it to crumble to ash in his hand before he can pass it to them.
The character’s breath briefly fogs up a mirror to spell 'run' before fading away.
A moth with a tiny skull pattern on its wings lands on their hand and remains still, as if staring at them.
The character’s name appears scratched into a tree near their haven, with no indication of how long it’s been there.
A mannequin in a shop window mimics their every move as they walk by.
The character notices flickering lights in the windows of an abandoned hospital every night at the same time.
A cracked pocket watch keeps appearing near their haven, frozen at 4:17 AM.
In the park, the character stumbles upon a meticulously arranged pile of bones that forms the shape of an eye.
A black feather floats down onto the character’s shoulder whenever they pass a particular bridge.
A stranger hands them an acorn, whispering, 'For luck,' before vanishing without a trace.
The character dreams of an old friend every night, only to wake with an inexplicable sense of dread.
An antique doll with glass eyes sits in front of their door one evening, facing directly at them.
Their reflection in the mirror occasionally mouths words they aren’t saying, staring back with a knowing look.
A crow caws three times whenever the character leaves their haven at dusk.
